operations.summary: read one JSON input file a command was named and decode it into the type the command reads

causes.cause: no file is at that path
causes.remedy: name a file that exists, or write it first; a relative path is read from {cwd}

causes.cause: the file exists but this process may not read it
causes.remedy: let the user running the command read it (chmod u+r {path}), or run the command as its owner

causes.cause: the path names a directory, not a file
causes.remedy: name the JSON file inside it, not the directory

causes.cause: the file opened but the operating system stopped the read part way, so the bytes in hand are not the whole file
causes.remedy: run the command again once the disk or the network share holding {path} answers; `ls -l {path}` shows whether it is still there

causes.cause: the file is not JSON: at line {line}, column {column} it holds a character JSON does not allow there
causes.observed: {bytes} bytes, line {line} reads {quoted_line}; the decoder answered {error}
causes.remedy: write valid JSON at line {line} of {path}, or name the file the command expects; `jq . {path}` shows the same place

causes.cause: the JSON ends before its last value closes, so the file is cut short or still being written
causes.observed: {bytes} bytes, ending at line {line}, column {column}; the decoder answered {error}
causes.remedy: finish writing {path}, or write it again whole, before running the command

causes.cause: the file is JSON but not the document the command reads: a field is missing, extra, or of another type
causes.observed: at line {line}, column {column}; the decoder answered {error}
causes.remedy: give the document the fields {expected} declares, or name the file meant for this command

operations.summary: print a command's result as pretty JSON, or with --text as one path: value line per field, from the same document

causes.failed: turning the result of type {type} into JSON
causes.cause: the result holds a value JSON has no form for, such as a map whose keys are not text
causes.remedy: give {type} keys that serialize as strings, or a Serialize form that writes them as text

causes.failed: writing {bytes} bytes of the result to standard output
causes.cause: whatever read standard output closed it before the result was written
causes.remedy: keep the reading end open until the command ends, as in `command | jq .` rather than a reader that stops early

causes.failed: writing {bytes} bytes of the result to standard output
causes.cause: the operating system refused the write for a reason other than a closed reader: a full disk behind a redirect, or a device gone
causes.remedy: free space on the disk standard output is redirected to, or redirect it elsewhere, and run the command again
